summary.oneLiner: A clean, seasonally-soft opening quarter that still delivered **+48% YoY revenue (INR466 cr), record order inflow (INR972 cr) and record order book (INR3,117 cr)** — with the whole thesis pivoting to the **imminent EHV inflection**: Vadod won its **Power Grid 400kV approval** this quarter, the first 400kV short-circuit test is due this quarter, and the **765kV tech tie-up (USD 3–5 mn + 2–4% royalty) is in final talks** with PGCIL 765kV approval "certainly" expected by Q2-end. FY27 guidance held at **40% revenue growth, 17–18% EBITDA margin.**

one-line thesis: A clean, seasonally-soft opening quarter that still delivered +48% YoY revenue (INR466 cr), record order inflow (INR972 cr) and record order book (INR3,117 cr) — with the whole thesis pivoting to the imminent EHV inflection: Vadod won its Power Grid 400kV approval this quarter, the first 400kV short-circuit test is due this quarter, and the 765kV tech tie-up (USD 3–5 mn + 2–4% royalty) is in final talks with PGCIL 765kV approval "certainly" expected by Q2-end. FY27 guidance held at 40% revenue growth, 17–18% EBITDA margin.
financial scorecard: Seasonality is the QoQ story: Q1 is structurally soft (tenders float early in the FY; execution/revenue is H2-heavy; capital-goods customers accelerate procurement at FY-end to use capex budgets). Q1FY27's 16.5% EBITDA margin is nonetheless the highest-ever Q1 (FY25 Q1: 13.8%, FY26 Q1: 15.48%).

Volume vs price: growth is volume-led + pure pass-through — per-MVA realisation is flat across KV classes (price-variation clauses pass RM inflation straight through; "no material change in pricing or mix" beyond the 220kV shift).
Installed capacity 63,060 MVA; Q1 utilization only 4,381 MVA (large seasonal headroom). Vadod produced 1,520 MVA, Ankhi/Jambusar 320 MVA this quarter.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter: Revenue: 40% growth FY27 (FY26 base INR 1,851 cr → ~INR 2,590 cr implied); 40% CAGR maintained for 3 years (FY27–29) with stable margins.
EBITDA margin: 17–18% for FY27 ("as we always convey") — up from the 16–16.5% IPO-time framing (FY26 landed at 18.52%).
Order execution: ~INR 2,400 cr of the INR 3,100 cr book executable in FY27.

765kV: PGCIL approval by end-Q2FY27 ("Certainly"); tech tie-up to close in Q2, RM injection/production Q3, bidding doors open by Q4FY27 (end of this FY). Uses Ankhi facility; needs PGCIL revalidation in new name.
400kV: first-unit short-circuit test this quarter; balance of the 315 MVA order executes within FY27; meaningful commercial 400kV contribution from FY28.
IDT facility (Unit 6): commission by Dec-2026 / Q3FY27, adds ~5,000 MVA.
Tank & radiator backward-integration facility: live by end-CY2026.
Exports: ~15% of revenue within 3 years (revenue stream from FY28); one export order in hand.
order book & pipeline: Record inflow INR 972.42 cr; book INR 3,116.63 cr (30-Jun-2026). Key wins: RVPNL (Rajasthan) INR 291.68 cr (160/50/31.5 MVA); PSTCL (Punjab) INR 285.15 cr (23× 160 MVA, 220/66kV).
Book mix moving up-voltage: 220kV >55% of book; 400kV transformers & reactors ~INR 275 cr (a first meaningful EHV slice). Entire record book is still "technically 220kV and below."
Order booking peaks Q2 → mid-Q3; mgmt expects "good amount of orders" to keep adding.
PGCIL Ultra-Mega orders (a peer just won >INR 1,000 cr) are "not one-off" — huge Power Grid backlog; Atlanta positions to crack 400kV PGCIL orders once product-development (Q2) ends.
segment / subsidiary: Revenue by product: power transformers ~79%; auto/IDT/others the balance. By KV: 220kV 56%, 66kV 25%, 132kV ~5.5%. By end-market: T&D ~66%, renewable ~19%, thermal + industrial the rest.
Vadod (Unit 4): now Power Grid 400kV-approved (milestone this quarter); also in PGCIL vendor-dev program for 500 MVA 400kV; will make the INR 275 cr 400kV book.
Ankhi/Jambusar (Unit 5, ex-BTW): the designated 765kV (and 400kV) site; still making 220kV in the interim.
growth verticals / optionality: 765kV platform — tech tie-up (undisclosed partner, held up by counterpart-govt tech-transfer approvals) at final stage; USD 3–5 mn one-time fee + 2–4% royalty for 3–4 years (765kV only). First 765kV transformer/ICT/reactor on Ankhi, then type tests, then order bidding by Q4FY27.
IDT (Unit 6) — dedicated facility, +5,000 MVA by Dec-2026; feeds renewable, BESS, EV-charging. Mgmt sees supply deficit across all ranges incl. IDT — reason for the dedicated plant.
Exports — 15% target in 3 years (Europe/Africa/US), framed explicitly as overcapacity-risk insurance + a lever to protect lower-kV margins.
Data centers — no order yet in the book, but a named structural demand driver.
6a. moat & competitive position (optiona: EHV first-mover / approval barrier: Vadod is now PGCIL 400kV-approved and Atlanta has a 220kV track record; mgmt argues new-entrant peers adding 400kV capacity still face multi-year approval + no supply history ("they will be still behind us"). Entry barriers + approval cycles are the durable edge.
765kV via exclusive tech tie-up — a licensed technology + PGCIL revalidation combination few domestic peers hold.
Price-variation pass-through on large transformers structurally protects gross margin from RM/CRGO/oil volatility — evidenced this quarter (flat per-MVA realisation despite RM inflation).
margins & cost dynamics: Record Q1 margin (16.5%) on operating leverage + 220kV mix; FY27 guided 17–18%. Job-to-job RM procurement (explicitly "not speculating on RM price"); price-variation clauses pass through inflation.
Mineral-oil shortage eased (had used ester/natural-oil contracts); oil prices now correcting down.

CRGO DGTR anti-dumping investigation — verdict expected ~end-March 2027; no near-term price/supply pressure; BIS licenses to some Chinese CRGO mills easing in ~1 month. 400/765kV margins expected higher than 220kV but mgmt won't quote until first prototype is built (tech-tie-up/dev costs will partly offset → net "stable").
capex / expansion (watch slippage): IDT Unit 6 (+5,000 MVA) by Dec-2026; tank & radiator BI facility (INR 180 cr total, only ~INR 15–20 cr spent so far) live by end-CY2026 — tank/radiators are 4–5% of transformer cost (modest BI scope).
400kV/765kV are the gating milestones; 400kV short-circuit test this quarter is the key near-term checkpoint.
capital allocation: Working capital tight & stable: NWC 72 days (inv 105, recv 88, pay 110); cash-conversion ~83 days despite scale-up. Inventory build is for the coming quarter's orders, not a full-year speculative stock.

765kV tech fee (USD 3–5 mn + royalty) and BI/IDT capex funded — mgmt didn't flag fresh equity; capex modest relative to scale. No dividend/buyback discussed (growth-stage, recently IPO'd ~9 months ago).
risks & watch-items: Industry overcapacity — peers (CG Power, Transformers & Rectifiers) adding ~60,000 MVA on 400kV in 3–4 months; mgmt sees no pricing pressure yet but flags it as the 1-year-out risk (mitigated via exports + EHV/new products).

Chinese players in PSU tenders — 4 firms cleared (only 1 makes transformers); mgmt sees limited near-term threat (that plant is busy with private Adani/Reliance orders, "no logic" to chase low-margin PSU work); no participation witnessed yet — monitor.
CRGO anti-dumping duty (verdict ~Mar-2027) — potential RM-cost inflation.
EHV execution/approval slippage — 765kV depends on a still-unsigned tech tie-up + counterpart-govt approvals; 400kV commercial contribution is FY28, not FY27.
Seasonality optics — H1 always soft; the 40% FY27 growth is back-ended to H2 (execution risk if approvals/tests slip).
management quality / tone: Confident, granular and disciplined — gave exact MVA-by-plant, KV-mix, order values, tech-tie-up economics and multi-year margin history. Candidly refuses to quote 400/765kV margins until a prototype is proven ("not right to comment… we are yet to manufacture"). Repeatedly declines to disparage competitors. Four-person management (MD/CEO/CFO/COO) all fielded questions cohesively.
non-obvious takeaways: This is a 220kV story that's about to become an EHV story — the record book is "technically 220kV and below"; the re-rating optionality (400/765kV, larger/longer/higher-margin orders) is entirely ahead and gated by Q2 short-circuit tests + the 765kV tie-up.
The 765kV economics are now disclosed — USD 3–5 mn upfront + 2–4% royalty for 3–4 years; a modest price for entry into a segment dominated by MNCs, but the royalty will cap 765kV margins early.
Margin guide quietly raised — from the IPO-time 16–16.5% to 17–18% (FY26 printed 18.52%), even as mgmt verbally frames it as "stable."
Exports are defensive, not offensive — explicitly to hedge industry overcapacity 1–2 years out and protect lower-kV margins; no export revenue until FY28.
CG Power + T&R (TARIL) 60,000 MVA of new 400kV capacity is the key sector watch-item — Atlanta's answer is speed-to-approval (already 400kV-approved) + product differentiation, not price.
qoq change log: Q1FY27 (this): Revenue INR 466 cr (+48% YoY, -37.6% QoQ on seasonality); EBITDA margin 16.5% (record Q1, normalised from ~20% Q4FY26); PAT INR 46.84 cr (+50.4%), EPS INR 6.09. Record inflow INR 972 cr → record book INR 3,116.63 cr (up from INR 2,451 cr in Q3FY26); ~INR 2,400 cr executable FY27. Volume 4,381 MVA (+21.5% YoY) vs 63,060 MVA capacity. Vadod won PGCIL 400kV approval (milestone); 400kV order book INR 275 cr; first 400kV short-circuit test due this quarter, commercial from FY28. 765kV tech tie-up final-stage (USD 3–5 mn + 2–4% royalty), PGCIL approval by Q2-end, orders open Q4FY27. IDT Unit 6 by Dec-2026 (+5,000 MVA); tank/radiator BI live end-CY26 (~INR 15–20/180 cr spent). FY27 guide: 40% rev growth (40% CAGR 3 yrs), 17–18% EBITDA margin. Exports 15% of revenue in 3 yrs (from FY28). Mineral-oil shortage eased; CRGO anti-dumping verdict ~Mar-2027.

next → check: 400kV short-circuit test pass + 315 MVA execution; 765kV PGCIL approval by Q2-end + tech tie-up signed; IDT Unit 6 Dec-2026 commissioning; H2 revenue ramp toward 40% FY27; margin holds 17–18%; order inflow Q2–mid-Q3 peak; first export order booking; CRGO duty outcome.

themes.title: Transformer & grid-component shortage
themes.need: Transformer makers are running flat-out at record order books even as core-capacity ramps land (ATLANTAELE 16k->63k MVA, Q1FY27 record order book INR3,117cr on record INR972cr quarterly inflow, Vadod now PGCIL 400kV-approved with a 765kV tech tie-up in final talks; TARIL toward 75k+ MVA, Q1FY27 UEOB INR6,630cr +26% YoY on a >INR1,000cr single-shot PGCIL Ultra-Mega order, though a Changodar-expansion air-pocket held Q1 revenue to +10%; SHILCTECH adding 220kV) yet the binding constraint is still everything INSIDE a transformer - CRGO core steel, CTC/winding wire (KSHINTL/BHAGYANGR), bushings/insulators (YASHHV; 18-24mo lead, ~95% RIP/OIP imported) and transformer oil (APARINDS); both OEMs are now backward-integrating to own the bottleneck (TARIL's INR900-1,000cr CRGO/CTC/bushing/pressboard programme). Capacity-gated supply is the repeated 'need of the hour' and is driving pricing power now, though both OEMs flagged ~60,000 MVA of new 400kV capacity landing industry-wide in 3-4 months as a 1-year-out overcapacity watch-item (neither sees pricing pressure yet).
themes.driver: PGCIL Ultra-Mega order conversion (TARIL's first >INR1,000cr single-shot award) + Vadod/Changodar capacity ramps; 400kV short-circuit tests and 765kV PGCIL approvals due by Q2FY27-end are the next re-rating triggers; TARIL's Changodar restart (Aug-2026) is the swing quarter for its own growth reacceleration.
